outcome: rate of psychotropic medication use during pregnancy
prevalence of psychotropic medication use during pregnancy
incidence of psychotropic medication use during pregnancy
associated psychiatric diagnoses (major depressive disorder, anxiety, adjustment reaction/acute stress)
cohort: The study included 424,307 pregnancies ending in a live birth in the Canadian province of British Columbia between January 1, 1997 and December 31, 2010.
finding: 7.1% of pregnancies involved the dispensing of psychotropic medication, with antidepressants (4.2%) and anxiolytics (3.4%) being the most common, suggesting a need to improve access to nondrug options before and during pregnancy.
